title: Add performance fingerprint signoffs and release capsule generator
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: reduce manual effort and human error when promoting onboarded models by automatically capturing a compact performance fingerprint, requiring an approver signoff for stability regressions, and bundling a concise release capsule for downstream consumers. This PR introduces: 1) a deterministic performance fingerprint computed from a trimmed set of latency/throughput/quality metrics and the serialized profile hash; 2) a signoff workflow that gates model promotion when fingerprint drift exceeds thresholds, integrating with the existing intake review queue; 3) a release capsule generator that composes a one-page JSON brief (human-readable blurb, delta summary, notable metric diffs, and suggested rollout cadence) and attaches it to model version releases; 4) CI hooks and a lightweight reviewer UI flag to record signoff comments and rationale. The description below summarizes changes, test coverage, and rollout plan. Checklist: [x] compute fingerprint algorithm and add unit tests, [x] expose fingerprint and drift score in intake API, [x] signoff workflow + reviewer comments capture, [x] release capsule builder + brief template, [x] CI lint/build/test passes on rerun, [x] migration that backfills fingerprints for recent onboarded models (30-day window) (migration included). Backwards compatibility: the fingerprint is additive metadata; promotion flows fall back to previous behavior when the feature flag is disabled. Rollout: feature-flagged rollout to staging for two weeks, followed by gradual enable on 25%, 50%, 100% of intake traffic. Related work: follows ENG-2187 (perf inference stability) and PM-342 (release brief UX).

review_comments: Ethan Chen: Can you quantify expected false positive drift rate for benign variance? Please add a short note in the doc and a test that simulates noisy latency samples.
Maya Patel (author): Added noise-simulation unit test and a short explanation in docs; tuned the drift threshold to reduce FP rate on our sampled workloads.
Lina Rodriguez: Security question: where is the release capsule stored and who can view it? We need to ensure private builds don't leak into public registry exports.

Maya Patel (author): Capsules are stored as model-version attachments in the private registry bucket with the same ACLs as existing profiles. Added a note in docs and an integration test asserting ACLs are respected.
Arjun Kapoor: NIT: consider making the brief template pluggable for enterprise customers. Also ensure the migration is idempotent.
Maya Patel (author): Made template loader configurable via registry config and made migration check for existing fingerprint before writing.

release_notes: Add performance fingerprint metadata, signoff gating for fingerprint drift, and automatic release capsule generation. Includes migration to backfill fingerprints for recent models. No breaking changes. See docs/model-onboarding/release-capsule.md for usage and rollout controls.
notes: Operational runbook updated with actions for signoff rejections and recommended rollback cadence. Feature controllable by flag registry.feature_perf_capsule. Observability: new metrics perf_fingerprint_drift_score and release_capsule_generation_latency emitted to registry.namespace.metrics.
